plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink, set against dark leathery leaves. It thrives in woodland gardens and blooms in the depths of winter, often pushing through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to late winter (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic. Legend says it sprang up from the tears of a girl who had no gift for the Christ child.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose showy colored bracts, not true petals, surround tiny yellow flowers called cyathia. In frost-free climates it grows into a large landscape shrub several meters tall, flowering as the days shorten.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter (December to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in tropical and subtropical regions and as a holiday houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants that need long uninterrupted nights to color up. The Aztecs used them to make a reddish dye and called them cuetlaxochitl.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like leaves that becomes covered in clusters of brilliant orange-red blossoms. Each flower has one petal streaked with white and yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere tropics and subtropics, including December in places such as northern Australia, and in some tropical regions with a long flowering period
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; cultivated in tropical regions including Australia, the Caribbean, India, and Africa
plants.funFact: The species is endangered in its native Madagascar even though it is among the most widely planted ornamental trees in the tropics.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: A glossy-leaved evergreen shrub that produces rose-like flowers with many layered petals. Many cultivars bloom in the cool months, brightening winter gardens when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; grown in mild temperate gardens in the southeastern United States, Europe, Japan, and elsewhere
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the source of all true tea. Camellia japonica is a symbol of winter and enduring love in Japan, where it is called tsubaki.
